spec_features.feature_name: termination on submit / max_steps / max_tool_calls / error
spec_features.spec_quote: End on `submit`, on a step budget (`max_steps`), on a tool-call cap (`max_tool_calls`), or on error
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:140 `for step_idx in range(config.max_steps)` bounds the loop (max_steps=25, loop.py:70); submit at loop.py:155-161 sets stop_reason='submit' and breaks; loop.py:177-179 `if total_tool_calls >= config.max_tool_calls: stop_reason='budget'; break` (max_tool_calls=80, loop.py:73); except Exception at loop.py:189-191 sets stop_reason='error'. All four are checked and actually change/terminate execution.
spec_features.notes: All four stop conditions are genuinely enforced and end the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Hard cap on total tool calls to avoid pathological loops. (loop.py:72)

spec_features.feature_name: one nudge on no-op turn then end
spec_features.spec_quote: a no-op turn gets one nudge before ending
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:180-188: on `turn.is_terminal_text` (no tool calls) it appends a user nudge message ('If you are finished, call `submit`...'). The nudge is genuinely wired and delivered. BUT the comment claims 'nudge once, then end to avoid infinite no-op loops' (loop.py:181) while the code does NOT end after nudging: there is no break and no flag tracking that a nudge was already issued, so every no-op turn is nudged again. Termination of repeated no-op turns relies solely on the generic max_steps bound, not on a 'one nudge then end' mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Nudge text really executes (real enforcement of the nudge); the 'then end' / 'once' part of the claim is not implemented as a dedicated mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # nudge once, then end to avoid infinite no-op loops. (loop.py:181)

spec_features.spec_quote: submit` is the explicit terminal act that yields the final report
spec_features.evidence: submit tool advertised at tools.py:79-91; in loop.py:155-161 a `submit` call sets final_summary=arguments['summary'], records {'status':'submitted'}, sets stop_reason='submit', and breaks the loop. final_summary is carried in the returned Transcript (loop.py:204). The exit is dispatched by the model and honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: The model can end the session at will via submit; honored end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: submit      (final answer; ends the loop) (tools.py docstring) -- neutral mechanics, no welfare reasoning in code
